concepts.why: The patient has a positive urinalysis and blood and urine cultures that grow Escherichia coli, which supports the diagnosis of a urinary tract infection.
The patient has symptoms of fever, flank pain, and leukocytosis, which are consistent with pyelonephritis, a type of kidney infection.
The patient has symptoms of foul-smelling urine and a positive urinalysis, which are consistent with cystitis, a type of bladder infection.
The patient has a CT scan that shows a non-obstructing right nephrolithiasis, which supports the diagnosis of kidney stones.
The patient has a CT scan that shows irregular, nodular thickening of the bladder wall, which is suspicious for neoplasm and supports the diagnosis of bladder cancer.
The patient has a history of severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, which is relevant to their current presentation.
The patient has a history of hypertension, which is relevant to their current presentation.
The patient has blood and urine cultures that grow Escherichia coli, which supports the diagnosis of an E. coli infection.

rationales.F01: Fever is a common symptom of urinary tract infections, pyelonephritis, and cystitis.
rationales.F02: Left-sided flank pain is a common symptom of pyelonephritis and nephrolithiasis.
rationales.F03: Foul-smelling urine is a common symptom of urinary tract infections, particularly cystitis.
rationales.F04: Bilateral lung transplantation is a significant risk factor for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
rationales.F05: Hypertension is a common comorbidity with many conditions, including urinary tract infections.
rationales.F06: A 70-pack-year smoking history is a significant risk factor for bladder cancer and COPD.
rationales.F07: Leukocytosis is a common laboratory finding in urinary tract infections and other bacterial infections.
